title: Fibre-associated generalizations detect relative flatness at a scheme point
statement: Let $f:V\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $N$ be a finite type quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Fix $v\in V$ and put $t=f(v)$. Let $i_t:V_t\to V$ be the scheme-theoretic fibre projection [def-pc-scheme-fibre], put $N_t=i_t^*N$ [def-pc-module-pullback], and regard $v$ as its corresponding point in $V_t$. Associated points of $N_t$ are [def-trf-relative-assassin]: a point $a$ is associated when the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{V_t,a}$ is the annihilator of a nonzero element of $(N_t)_a$. Say that $a$ specializes to $v$ when $v\in\overline{\{a\}}$ in $V_t$. Then $N_v$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ if and only if $N_a$ is flat over $\mathcal O_{T,t}$ for every $a\in\operatorname{Ass}_{V_t}(N_t)$ specializing to $v$. Here $N_a$ denotes the stalk on $V$ at the image of $a$, and both base actions are induced by $f$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. No Noetherian, quasi-compactness, separation, finite-presentation, or flatness hypothesis on $T$ or $f$ is imposed.

proof.text: Put $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, $B=\mathcal O_{V,v}$ and $P=N_v$. Fix an affine neighbourhood $W=\operatorname{Spec}R$ of $v$ on which $N=\widetilde L$, and let $\mathfrak r$ represent $v$. The canonical local-spectrum morphism identifies local rings at all generalizations of $v$; the tilde-stalk formula gives $B=R_{\mathfrak r}$ and $P=L_{\mathfrak r}$. If $a$ generalizes $v$, represented by $\mathfrak s\subseteq\mathfrak r$, it follows that $N_a=L_{\mathfrak s}=P_{\mathfrak sB}$. The last module identification sends $(l/s)/(r/u)$ to $ul/(sr)$; the fraction equality criterion gives its inverse. For $a$ in $V_t$ these are $A$-linear identifications via $f$. Therefore, if $P$ is $A$-flat, localization preserves this flatness, proving the forward implication, even for every generalization in the fibre.

source.place: Tag 05UA (theorem-check-flatness-at-associated-points), first sentence of proof; affine stalks from Tag 01HV (lemma-spec-sheaves).

proof.text: For the converse suppose the stated flatness at associated generalizations. The stalk map $A\to B$ is a local homomorphism essentially of finite type, and $P$ is finite over $B$. Write $B=W_0^{-1}D$ for a finite type $A$-algebra $D$. Put $k=A/\mathfrak m_A$, $C=B/\mathfrak m_AB$ and $\overline P=P/\mathfrak m_AP$. The fraction maps $[d/w]\mapsto[d]/[w]$ and $[d]/[w]\mapsto[d/w]$ identify $C$ with the localization of $D/\mathfrak m_AD$ at the image of $W_0$. The latter algebra is finite type over $k$, generated by the images of generators of $D$. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and itself. Finite type algebras over Noetherian rings and their localizations are Noetherian, so $C$ is Noetherian. The images of a finite $B$-generating list for $P$ generate $\overline P$ over $C$. No Noetherianity of $A$ or $B$ has been used.

source.place: Tag 05UA, reduction to the local rings and finite stalk; verification of Tag 05DE hypotheses using Tag 00FN (lemma-Noetherian-permanence).

proof.text: The fibre-stalk quotient identifies $C$ with $\mathcal O_{V_t,v}$, and the pullback-stalk formula identifies $\overline P$ with $(N_t)_v$, by $p\otimes[b]\mapsto[bp]$. Pullback preserves quasi-coherence, so the affine calculation of Step 1 applies also to $N_t$ on $V_t$. Let $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(\overline P)$ and let $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ be its image in $C$; it exists since $\mathfrak m_AB$ kills $\overline P$. Choose $z\ne0$ with $\operatorname{Ann}_B(z)=\mathfrak q$. Then $\operatorname{Ann}_C(z)=\overline{\mathfrak q}$. Under the canonical map $\operatorname{Spec}C\to V_t$, this prime gives a generalization $a$ of $v$, with fibre stalk $(N_t)_a=(\overline P)_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}$. The element $z/1$ is nonzero: an element outside $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ cannot kill $z$. Its annihilator is $\overline{\mathfrak q}C_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}$: if $(c/s)(z/1)=0$, some $h\notin\overline{\mathfrak q}$ has $hcz=0$, whence $c\in\overline{\mathfrak q}$ by primality; the reverse inclusion follows from $\overline{\mathfrak q}z=0$. Thus $a$ is associated on the fibre under the stated definition. Its image in $V$ corresponds to $\mathfrak q\subset B$: both local-spectrum maps send each affine function to its germ and then its quotient class, so contraction of $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is $\mathfrak q$. Step 1 identifies $P_{\mathfrak q}=N_a$ as $A$-modules; hence $P_{\mathfrak q}$ is $A$-flat by hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 05UA, translating assumption (2) to associated primes of the local closed-fibre module; Tags 0HA1 (lemma-local-ring-fibre), 0098 (lemma-stalk-pullback-modules).

proof.text: Let $\Sigma\subset B$ be the elements acting injectively on $\overline P$, put $B'=\Sigma^{-1}B$, and put $M=\Sigma^{-1}P$. The set is multiplicative because the identity acts injectively and compositions of injective scalar multiplications are injective. Apply the closed-fibre regular-localization spectrum lemma to $A\to B$ and $P$: Step 2 gives precisely its Noetherian closed-fibre ring and finite closed-fibre module. Every prime $\mathfrak p'$ of $B'$ contracts to a prime $\mathfrak p\subset B$ contained in some $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Ass}_B(\overline P)$.

For such $\mathfrak p'$, the corresponding localizations satisfy $M_{\mathfrak p'}=P_{\mathfrak p}$: every element of $\Sigma$ is outside $\mathfrak p$, and successive fractions identify by $(p/s)/(b/t)\mapsto tp/(sb)$. Since $\mathfrak p\subseteq\mathfrak q$, $P_{\mathfrak p}$ is a localization of $P_{\mathfrak q}$ (the same fraction formula, inverting $B\setminus\mathfrak p$). Step 3 and preservation of base flatness by module localization imply $M_{\mathfrak p'}$ is $A$-flat. If $\mathfrak a$ is the contraction of $\mathfrak p'$ to $A$, this module has its natural $A_{\mathfrak a}$-action and flatness over $A$ agrees with flatness over $A_{\mathfrak a}$. Apply the existing affine local flatness criterion to $A\to B'$ and $M$, for all primes $\mathfrak p'$: it gives $M$ flat over $A$. This also covers $B'=0$, since the criterion allows an empty spectrum.

source.place: Tag 05UA, conclusion that the localized module is base-flat, expanded with Algebra Tag 00HT (lemma-flat-localization), parts (2) and (6).

proof.text: The map $u:P\to M$, $p\mapsto p/1$, is $B$-linear. There is a canonical quotient comparison $M/\mathfrak m_AM\cong\Sigma^{-1}\overline P$, $[p/s]\mapsto[p]/s$. Its inverse sends $[p]/s$ to $[p/s]$: changing $p$ by a sum $\sum a_ip_i$ with $a_i\in\mathfrak m_A$ changes the image by $\sum a_i(p_i/s)$; equalities of fractions are checked by multiplying a common denominator. Both composites are the identity on fractions. Under this comparison the reduction of $u$ is $\overline P\to\Sigma^{-1}\overline P$. If $[p]/1=0$, the localization kernel criterion gives $s[p]=0$ for some $s\in\Sigma$; by the definition of $\Sigma$, this implies $[p]=0$. Thus the reduction of $u$ modulo $\mathfrak m_A$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 05UA, injectivity modulo the maximal ideal, from the localization fraction definition.

proof.text: Apply the finite-source fibre-injective flat-target lemma to $A\to B$ and $u:P\to M$. Step 2 supplies the local essentially finite type ring map and the finite $B$-module $P$. Step 5 gives $A$-flatness of $M$, and Step 6 gives exactly the required injection $P/\mathfrak m_AP\to M/\mathfrak m_AM$. The lemma requires no finiteness of $M$ or locality of its scalar extension $B'$. It follows that $P=N_v$ is flat over $A=\mathcal O_{T,t}$, proving the converse.

tool_uses.why: The local-spectrum image and stalk identifications provide the scheme-to-local-algebra translation; no lemma in this unit gives them.
Preservation of relative module flatness under source localization is a generic algebra tool, needed for both the forward implication and the localized prime tests.
Finite generation of the Zariski stalk is needed to apply 0AT4; the unit has no replacement for this generic sheaf fact.
The exact fibre local-ring quotient identifies the associated primes with fibre generalizations; no same-unit node supplies it.
The pullback-stalk tensor formula identifies the fibre module with the maximal-ideal quotient, without any base-flatness hypothesis.
Quasi-coherence after pullback allows the tilde-stalk calculation on the fibre, independent of flatness.

lean.statement: theorem flat_stalk_iff_associated_generizations {V T : Scheme.{u}} (f : V ⟶ T) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (N : V.Modules) (hN : N.IsQuasiCoherentFiniteType) (v : V) : Module.Flat (T.presheaf.stalk (f v)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars (f.stalkMap v).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor V.toRingedSpace v).obj N)) ↔ ∀ a : f.fiber (f v), a ∈ associatedPoints ((tensorPullback (f.fiberι (f v))).obj N) → a ⤳ f.asFiber v → Module.Flat (T.presheaf.stalk (f v)) ((ModuleCat.restrictScalars ((T.presheaf.stalkCongr (.of_eq (f.fiberHomeo (f v) a).property)).inv ≫ f.stalkMap (f.fiberι (f v) a)).hom).obj ((RingedSpace.moduleStalkFunctor V.toRingedSpace (f.fiberι (f v) a)).obj N))

reviewed_lean.note: Statement matches Stacks 05UA and the node clause by clause: locally finite type f; quasi-coherent finite-type N (IsQuasiCoherentFiniteType); fibre N_t via tensorPullback(fiberι); exact-annihilator associatedPoints; a ⤳ asFiber v in the right direction; flatness of the original V-stalks over O_{T,f v}, the right-hand side via the canonical stalkCongr(.of_eq fiberHomeo.property).inv ≫ stalkMap. No extra hypotheses; one universe; split fields identical to live except the new lean field; imports are the stmt_dep and proof_dep records; docstrings carry source, blueprint tag and 7 proof steps; proof is sorry only; report sections present. Edge cases N=0, empty V, reflexive specialization, non-Noetherian base, Z_(p) with A/p all correct.
